study_identification_part.si4_title: Charting brain growth and aging at high spatial precision

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Assemble a large multi-site reference cohort and fit normative models of cortical thickness and subcortical volume across the lifespan; validate performance and demonstrate clinical utility by applying models to a transdiagnostic psychiatric sample and transfer to new sites.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Group comparisons using percent extreme deviations vs. matched controls and mass-univariate t-tests with FDR correction on both raw measures and deviation scores (case–control effects).
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Lifespan normative reference models of cortical thickness and subcortical volumes trained on 58,836 participants across 82 sites fit well and transfer to new sites; deviation maps reveal transdiagnostic heterogeneity and add information beyond standard case–control analyses.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: The authors assembled a multi-site lifespan cohort (N=58,836; ages 2–100) and fit warped Bayesian linear regression models per parcel (Destrieux atlas) to derive centiles and deviation scores for cortical thickness and subcortical volumes (FreeSurfer v6.0). Models were validated on a manually quality-checked subset (mQC N=24,354), across resampled site-stratified test splits, in a transdiagnostic clinical sample (N=1,985), and on a different-domain transfer dataset (OpenNeuro; six sites; N=546). Evaluation metrics (EV, MSLL, skew, kurtosis) indicate good fit to central tendency, variance, and distributional shape across regions. In clinical applications, maps of extreme deviations (|Z|>2) differed across disorders and individuals, and results from deviation-based analyses provided complementary information to mass-univariate case–control tests.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: Models, code, and documentation are openly shared, including tutorial notebooks and an example transfer dataset from new sites to facilitate applying the pretrained reference models to users' data.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: Sampling bias due to aggregation of existing studies (e.g., UK Biobank contributes 59% of the full sample; WEIRD bias likely); reliance on semi-automated QC for the full sample (despite conservative thresholds); FreeSurfer not adjusted for very young ages (2–7 years), warranting caution when applying models in that range; terminology preference for 'reference cohort' over 'normative model'.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: Datasets explicitly listed include ABCD; ABIDE; ADHD200; CAMCAN; CMI-HBN; HCP-Aging; HCP-Development; HCP-Early Psychosis; HCP-Young Adult; IXI; NKI-RS; OASIS; OpenNeuro; PNC; SRPBS; UK Biobank; plus multiple institutional cohorts (UMich, UCDavis/MIND, Oslo/NORMENT, KCL, Amsterdam UMC). Full per-site counts, ages, and sex are in Supplementary files 1–2; a transfer dataset from OpenNeuro (six sites; N=546) is provided for external validation.
